drugs.indications: Hypertension, Angina, Coronary Artery Disease
drugs.mechanism: Blocks L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle
drugs.clinicalPearls: Monitor for peripheral edema, avoid abrupt discontinuation, grapefruit interaction

drugs.indications: Hypertension, Angina, Myocardial Infarction, Arrhythmias
drugs.mechanism: Selective beta-1 adrenergic antagonist
drugs.clinicalPearls: Never abruptly stop, may cause rebound hypertension, monitor heart rate

drugs.indications: Hypertension, Heart Failure, Myocardial Infarction, Diabetic Nephropathy
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits ACE, reduces angiotensin II formation
drugs.clinicalPearls: Monitor potassium and creatinine, dry cough is common

drugs.indications: MI Prevention, Stroke Prevention, Angina, Acute Coronary Syndrome
drugs.mechanism: Irreversibly inhibits COX, reduces thromboxane A2
drugs.clinicalPearls: Use lowest effective dose, take with food to reduce GI upset

drugs.indications: Hyperlipidemia, Coronary Artery Disease Prevention, Post-MI
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, reduces cholesterol synthesis
drugs.clinicalPearls: Monitor liver function and CK, check lipid panel in 4-12 weeks

drugs.indications: Depression, Anxiety Disorders, OCD, PTSD, Panic Disorder
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits serotonin reuptake in presynaptic neurons
drugs.clinicalPearls: Takes 2-4 weeks for full effect, monitor for serotonin syndrome, sexual side effects

drugs.indications: Anxiety Disorders, Insomnia, Seizures, Alcohol Withdrawal, Agitation
drugs.mechanism: Enhances GABA inhibitory effects in CNS
drugs.clinicalPearls: High abuse potential, monitor for dependence, taper slowly on discontinuation

drugs.indications: Depression, Neuropathic Pain, Migraine Prevention, Chronic Pain
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits reuptake of norepinephrine and serotonin
drugs.clinicalPearls: Anticholinergic side effects common, especially in elderly, monitor cardiac function

drugs.indications: Type 2 Diabetes, Prediabetes, PCOS, Metabolic Syndrome
drugs.mechanism: Decreases hepatic glucose production, improves peripheral glucose uptake
drugs.clinicalPearls: First-line for Type 2 DM, monitor renal function annually, gastrointestinal side effects

drugs.indications: Type 1 Diabetes, Type 2 Diabetes, Hyperglycemia
drugs.mechanism: Binds to insulin receptor, promotes glucose uptake and utilization
drugs.clinicalPearls: Cannot be mixed, consistent timing essential, teach injection technique

drugs.indications: Hypothyroidism, Myxedema, Thyroid Cancer Suppression, Goiter
drugs.mechanism: Replaces deficient thyroid hormone T4
drugs.clinicalPearls: Take on empty stomach, check TSH annually, many drug interactions

drugs.indications: Asthma, COPD, Acute Bronchospasm, Exercise-induced Asthma
drugs.mechanism: Beta-2 adrenergic agonist, activates cAMP cascade
drugs.clinicalPearls: Use spacer with inhaler, increased use suggests poor control, monitor for rebound

drugs.indications: Asthma Maintenance, COPD, Allergic Rhinitis, Chronic Cough
drugs.mechanism: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist, reduces inflammatory mediators
drugs.clinicalPearls: Rinse mouth after use to prevent candidiasis, maintenance therapy essential

drugs.indications: COPD, Asthma, Chronic Bronchitis, Rhinorrhea
drugs.mechanism: Blocks acetylcholine receptors on smooth muscle
drugs.clinicalPearls: Slower onset than beta-2 agonists, good adjunct in COPD, avoid eye contact

drugs.indications: GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome, NSAID-induced Ulcer
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits H+/K+-ATPase pump in gastric parietal cells
drugs.clinicalPearls: Long-term use monitor B12, magnesium, and calcium, reduce duration if possible

drugs.indications: GERD, Gastroparesis, Nausea/Vomiting, Chemotherapy-induced Nausea
drugs.mechanism: Dopamine antagonist, enhances acetylcholine effects
drugs.clinicalPearls: Black box warning for tardive dyskinesia, use short-term only

drugs.indications: GERD, Peptic Ulcer, Gastritis, Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome
drugs.mechanism: Blocks H2 receptors on parietal cells, reduces acid secretion
drugs.clinicalPearls: Less effective than PPIs, fewer interactions than PPI, good safety profile

drugs.indications: Otitis Media, Sinusitis, Pneumonia, UTI, Skin Infections, Endocarditis Prophylaxis
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis
drugs.clinicalPearls: Check allergy history, may reduce oral contraceptive efficacy, common first-line agent

drugs.indications: Respiratory Infections, STIs, Atypical Pneumonia, Pertussis, Cat-scratch Disease
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit
drugs.clinicalPearls: Can cause QT prolongation, monitor EKG in high-risk patients, long half-life

drugs.indications: Skin Infections, UTI, Respiratory Infections, Bone Infections
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis
drugs.clinicalPearls: 5-10% cross-reactivity with penicillin allergy, safe in penicillin allergy if no history of anaphylaxis

drugs.indications: Arthritis, Muscle Pain, Fever, Dysmenorrhea, Headache, Post-operative Pain
drugs.mechanism: Non-selective inhibition of COX-1 and COX-2
drugs.clinicalPearls: Use lowest dose for shortest duration, take with food, avoid in pregnancy 3rd trimester

drugs.indications: Arthritis, Musculoskeletal Pain, Dysmenorrhea, Migraine, Chronic Pain
drugs.mechanism: Non-selective COX inhibition with longer duration
drugs.clinicalPearls: Longer half-life allows twice daily dosing, more GI toxicity than ibuprofen

drugs.indications: Muscle Spasm, Musculoskeletal Pain, Back Pain, Fibromyalgia
drugs.mechanism: CNS depression, reduces alpha-2 adrenergic activity
drugs.clinicalPearls: Causes sedation, avoid driving, short-term use recommended, take at bedtime

drugs.indications: Rheumatoid Arthritis, Osteoarthritis, Ankylosing Spondylitis, Post-operative Pain
drugs.mechanism: Non-selective COX inhibition, potent anti-inflammatory
drugs.clinicalPearls: More potent than ibuprofen, higher GI toxicity, avoid in elderly if possible

drugs.indications: Edema, Hypertension, Heart Failure, Pulmonary Edema, Ascites
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits Na-K-2Cl cotransporter in loop of Henle
drugs.clinicalPearls: Monitor potassium and renal function, ototoxicity with high doses, rapid onset

drugs.indications: Edema, Ascites, Heart Failure, Hypertension, Hypokalemia
drugs.mechanism: Aldosterone antagonist, blocks sodium reabsorption and potassium excretion
drugs.clinicalPearls: Monitor potassium closely, potassium-sparing agent, slow onset of action

drugs.indications: Hypokalemia, Potassium Replacement, Diuretic-induced Hypokalemia
drugs.mechanism: Replaces intracellular and extracellular potassium
drugs.clinicalPearls: Monitor serum K+ closely, take with food, never bolus IV, risk of hyperkalemia

drugs.indications: Atrial Fibrillation, DVT Prevention, PE Prevention, Valve Prosthesis, Post-MI
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits vitamin K-dependent clotting factors II, VII, IX, X
drugs.clinicalPearls: Monitor INR, narrow therapeutic window, many drug interactions

drugs.indications: ACS, Recent MI, Recent Stroke, Coronary Stent, PAD
drugs.mechanism: Irreversibly inhibits P2Y12 platelet receptor
drugs.clinicalPearls: Often used with aspirin, genetic variations affect response, PPI interaction

drugs.indications: Heart Failure, Atrial Fibrillation, Paroxysmal Atrial Tachycardia
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits Na-K-ATPase, increases intracellular calcium
drugs.clinicalPearls: Narrow therapeutic window, monitor levels, renal dosing needed

drugs.indications: Hypertension, Angina, MI, Arrhythmias, Essential Tremor, Hyperthyroidism
drugs.mechanism: Non-selective beta-1 and beta-2 adrenergic antagonist
drugs.clinicalPearls: Non-selective blocks beta-2, lipophilic crosses BBB, good for tremor

drugs.indications: Hypertension, Angina, SVT, Atrial Fibrillation
drugs.mechanism: Non-selective calcium channel blocker with negative inotropic effects
drugs.clinicalPearls: Non-dihydropyridine has rate-limiting effects, good for SVT

drugs.indications: Hypertension, Heart Failure, Post-MI, Diabetic Nephropathy
drugs.mechanism: Blocks angiotensin II type 1 receptor
drugs.clinicalPearls: No cough like ACE inhibitors, monitor potassium and creatinine

drugs.indications: Depression, Anxiety, OCD, PTSD, Bulimia, Panic Disorder
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits serotonin reuptake
drugs.clinicalPearls: Long half-life, sexual side effects common, activating for some patients

drugs.indications: Depression, Anxiety, Panic Disorder, Neuropathic Pain, Migraine
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits reuptake of serotonin and norepinephrine
drugs.clinicalPearls: Dose-dependent norepinephrine effects, watch blood pressure, difficult withdrawal

drugs.indications: Anxiety, Insomnia, Muscle Spasm, Seizures, Alcohol Withdrawal, Agitation
drugs.mechanism: Enhances GABA inhibitory effects
drugs.clinicalPearls: Long half-life, active metabolites, high abuse potential

drugs.indications: Epilepsy, Generalized Tonic-Clonic Seizures, Status Epilepticus, Arrhythmias
drugs.mechanism: Blocks sodium channels, inhibits neuronal firing
drugs.clinicalPearls: Narrow therapeutic index, saturable kinetics, many drug interactions

drugs.indications: Epilepsy, Trigeminal Neuralgia, Bipolar Disorder, Neuropathic Pain
drugs.mechanism: Blocks sodium channels, stabilizes neuronal membrane
drugs.metabolism: Hepatic via CYP3A4, induces its own metabolism
drugs.clinicalPearls: Auto-induction over time, monitor CBC, Stevens-Johnson risk especially in Asians

drugs.indications: Parkinson's Disease, Restless Leg Syndrome, Parkinsonian Syndrome
drugs.mechanism: Converted to dopamine, crosses blood-brain barrier
drugs.metabolism: Peripheral conversion to dopamine, then metabolized
drugs.clinicalPearls: Always give with carbidopa/benserazide, dyskinesia worsens with time

drugs.indications: Schizophrenia, Psychosis, Agitation, Delirium, Tourette's, ADHD
drugs.mechanism: Blocks dopamine D2 receptors in brain
drugs.clinicalPearls: EPS common, monitor for neuroleptic malignant syndrome, lower potency = more sedation

drugs.indications: Schizophrenia, Bipolar Disorder, Autism Aggression, Psychosis
drugs.mechanism: Blocks dopamine D2 and serotonin 5HT2A receptors
drugs.clinicalPearls: Lower EPS than typical antipsychotics, weight gain/metabolic concerns, IM depot available

drugs.indications: Type 2 Diabetes
drugs.mechanism: Stimulates pancreatic beta cells to release insulin
drugs.clinicalPearls: Risk of hypoglycemia, weight gain, use with caution in elderly

drugs.indications: Type 2 Diabetes
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits dipeptidyl peptidase-4, prolongs incretin action
drugs.clinicalPearls: No hypoglycemia risk, weight neutral, good safety profile, renal dosing needed

drugs.indications: Type 2 Diabetes
drugs.mechanism: Activates PPAR-gamma, improves insulin sensitivity
drugs.clinicalPearls: Weight gain significant, fluid retention, increased fracture risk in women

drugs.indications: Type 2 Diabetes, Postprandial Hyperglycemia
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits alpha-glucosidases, delays carbohydrate digestion
drugs.clinicalPearls: Take with first bite of meal, GI side effects very common, enzyme inhibitor

drugs.indications: Asthma, Allergic Rhinitis, Exercise-induced Asthma, Chronic Rhinosinusitis
drugs.mechanism: Blocks leukotriene D4 receptors in airways
contraindications: None absolute, but use cautiously with psychiatric history
drugs.clinicalPearls: Black box warning for neuropsychiatric effects, good for exercise-induced asthma

drugs.indications: Asthma Maintenance, COPD, Exercise-induced Asthma Prevention
drugs.mechanism: Long-acting beta-2 agonist, slow onset but long duration
drugs.clinicalPearls: ALWAYS use with inhaled corticosteroid, never monotherapy, slow onset 10-20 min

drugs.indications: GERD, Peptic Ulcer, NSAID-induced Ulcer, Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits H+/K+-ATPase pump
drugs.clinicalPearls: Similar to omeprazole, monitor for long-term complications

drugs.indications: GERD, Peptic Ulcer, Gastritis, Stress Ulcer Prevention
drugs.mechanism: Blocks H2 receptors on parietal cells
drugs.clinicalPearls: Twice daily dosing, fewer drug interactions than PPI, less effective than PPI

drugs.indications: C. difficile Infection, Giardia, Trichomoniasis, Anaerobic Infections, Bacterial Vaginosis
drugs.mechanism: Causes DNA strand breaks in organisms
drugs.clinicalPearls: Disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol, excellent for anaerobes and C. diff

drugs.indications: Respiratory Infections, STIs, Acne, Lyme Disease, Malaria Prophylaxis
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits bacterial 30S ribosomal subunit
drugs.clinicalPearls: Photosensitivity common, take with food, good for atypical infections

drugs.indications: Urinary Tract Infections, Respiratory Infections, GI Infections, Anthrax
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV
drugs.clinicalPearls: Broad spectrum, good oral absorption, tendon rupture risk especially in elderly

drugs.indications: Candida Infections, Cryptococcal Meningitis, Coccidioidomycosis
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits fungal cytochrome P450, disrupts cell membrane
drugs.clinicalPearls: Good CNS penetration, many drug interactions, monitor LFTs

drugs.indications: Herpes Simplex, Varicella-Zoster, Cytomegalovirus
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits viral DNA polymerase
drugs.clinicalPearls: Requires renal dosing, IV formulation for serious infections, hydration important

drugs.indications: Osteoarthritis, Rheumatoid Arthritis, Ankylosing Spondylitis
drugs.mechanism: Selective COX-2 inhibition
drugs.clinicalPearls: Once daily dosing, selective COX-2, long half-life

drugs.indications: Gout, Hyperuricemia, Uric Acid Stones, Cancer Chemotherapy
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits xanthine oxidase, reduces uric acid synthesis
drugs.clinicalPearls: Renal dosing needed, Stevens-Johnson risk, prophylactic NSAIDs with initiation

drugs.indications: Acute Gout Attacks, Gout Prophylaxis, FMF
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits microtubule polymerization, reduces neutrophil migration
drugs.clinicalPearls: Effective in first 24 hours of attack, many drug interactions, GI side effects

drugs.indications: Hypertension, Edema, Osteoporosis Prevention
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits Na-Cl cotransporter in distal convoluted tubule
drugs.clinicalPearls: First-line for hypertension, metabolic side effects at higher doses

drugs.indications: Edema, Hypertension, Hypokalemia
drugs.mechanism: Blocks epithelial sodium channels in collecting duct
drugs.clinicalPearls: Usually combined with loop or thiazide diuretic, monitor K+

drugs.indications: Cerebral Edema, Raised Intracranial Pressure, Acute Kidney Injury Prevention
drugs.mechanism: Osmotic diuretic, draws fluid into vasculature
drugs.clinicalPearls: IV only, rapid onset, monitor electrolytes, rebound effect possible
